revisions.why: The route this round built is the operator surface the provider-call-state round left open: retryJob refuses while a provider call is unreconciled, and until now the only way to clear one was to run a repository method against the real database by hand. Every guard on it fires only on state the happy path cannot reach -- a charge that is already known, a row somebody else resolved, an attempt D1 INTEGER affinity would silently convert from a string -- which is the exact shape that has beaten this project four times. PCS-29 is the one that matters most: without it a charged call can be relabelled abandoned through the public API in one request, which sets not_charged on a call that really was paid for and unblocks a retry that pays again. The table CHECK does not refuse that transition, because the pair it produces is legal.

purpose: Mutation testing is the mechanism this workstream uses to decide whether a test suite can
detect wrong behaviour at all. It repeatedly found suites that were 100% green and provably
useless: 9 of 12 mutants survived the prompt compiler, and 9 of 23 survived the D1 schema,
Until this file existed the mutant set lived only as prose in agent reports inside a
gitignored directory. The most recent round had to reconstruct 28 mutants by hand from two
earlier write-ups. This manifest exists so a round's baseline can be VERIFIED rather than

applyOneMutant: 1. Confirm the suite named in `set.testCommand` is green first. A mutant run against a red
2. Take `mutation.find` and `mutation.replace` and do a single literal string substitution
in `target.file`. `find` is byte-exact against the baseline commit and is verified to
occur exactly once in that file (`mutation.anchorUnique`).
'killed'         -> at least one test in `killedBy` MUST fail. If the suite is green,
the coverage this mutant guards has been lost. That is a finding.
'known-survivor' -> the suite is EXPECTED to stay green. A pass is not reassurance.
'retired'        -> do not apply. The behaviour it reverted no longer exists.
5. Restore the file (`git checkout -- <file>`) and re-confirm green before the next mutant.

readTheStatuses.killed: Measured as killed by the round named in `provenance.introducedIn`.
readTheStatuses.known-survivor: Measured as surviving. Either an accepted gap or one closed later by a successor; see `notes`.
readTheStatuses.retired: Deliberately withdrawn. Kept listed with reason, `retirement.kind` and successor; never deleted, because silently dropping a mutant hides a coverage loss. See `retirementKinds` — the two reasons for retiring are NOT the same thing and must not be conflated.
readTheStatuses.described-group: The round reported this as an aggregate of N mutations with a count but never enumerated them. Not individually applicable. Recorded so the count is not mistaken for enumerated evidence.

retirementKinds.why: A retired mutant can be retired for two materially different reasons, and collapsing them loses the more dangerous one. Every `retirement` block therefore carries a `kind`.
retirementKinds.behaviour-removed: The production behaviour the mutant reverted was deliberately deleted, so the mutation is no longer expressible. The code is GONE. DOM-14 is the only instance: ruling R6 deleted the reserved-prefix rule. Successor DOM-23.
retirementKinds.became-equivalent: The code is still there, but a change elsewhere made this mutation UNKILLABLE BY CONSTRUCTION — the mutated program is behaviourally identical to the original, so no test can ever fail and the mutant is not measuring anything. THIS IS THE DANGEROUS ONE: an equivalent mutant that is left in the set reads as a survivor and drags the score down for no reason, while an equivalent mutant that is quietly deleted hides the fact that a real check stopped being reachable. Neither is acceptable; it must be retired EXPLICITLY with this kind.
retirementKinds.noInstancesYet: No mutant in this manifest is retired as `became-equivalent`. One nearly was — see DOM-32R.equivalenceHazard, which is the worked example and the reason this vocabulary exists.
retirementKinds.howToSpotOne: The mutation applies cleanly, the suite is green, and inspection shows the mutated construct cannot affect behaviour on any input (typically because a second copy of the same check runs first). If the suite is green because coverage is MISSING, that is a known-survivor, not an equivalent mutant. Do not label one as the other: the first is a bug in the tests, the second is a fact about the program.

substantiationLevels.exact-from-source: The round described the mutant in one line; the literal find/replace here was derived by reading the target file at the baseline commit, and the anchor was verified unique. Applying it reproduces the described behaviour change.
substantiationLevels.described-only: The round's description is not specific enough to derive a faithful literal mutation without inventing detail. No find/replace is given. Do not guess one — treat the entry as a pointer to the report.
substantiationLevels.aggregate-only: Reported as a group count only.

equivalenceHazard.lesson: THIS MUTANT NEARLY BECAME AN EQUIVALENT MUTANT, AND THAT IS WHY THE `became-equivalent` RETIREMENT KIND EXISTS.
equivalenceHazard.detail: When the b69678b round lifted the entry-count bound in front of the array stage, the obvious-looking move was to LEAVE the old `.max(maximumEntries * RAW_ENTRY_SLACK)` on the array stage as free defence in depth. It would have been defence in depth in appearance only: sitting behind the new pre-bound it could never fire on any input, so no test could hold it honest — and mutating it would have produced a mutant that is UNKILLABLE BY CONSTRUCTION. The raw-bound set would then have read 7/8 with a survivor, while nothing was actually wrong.
equivalenceHazard.resolution: The round removed the second copy deliberately, precisely so DOM-32R stays a real, killable mutant. The source comment at b69678b says so: 'This is the ONLY raw entry-count bound. The array stage deliberately keeps no .max() of its own: a second copy of the same check sitting behind this one could never fire, so no test could hold it honest and no mutation to it could be caught.'
equivalenceHazard.generalRule: A duplicated guard behind an earlier guard is not redundancy — it is an unmeasurable region of the program. Before adding a backstop, ask whether any input can reach it; if none can, the mutant that targets it is equivalent, and a mutation score computed over it is fiction.

premise.claim: The kill signal is an element-parse count taken from accessor properties on a real array, and it is valid only while zod reads array elements in exactly ONE place — `[...ctx.data].map((item, i) => def.type._parseSync(...))` in ZodArray._parse (v3/types.js:1808).
premise.crossCheck: The suite asserts the correspondence indirectly: the accepted control sends n entries and observes exactly n reads, never 2n.
premise.failureMode: A future zod that pre-scanned the array for any other purpose would make the counter OVER-REPORT, and these tests would go red for a reason that is not a regression. The local-replica contract test ('zod keeps parsing elements after an array-side .max() has already failed') is what tells a reader which of the two happened.
premise.consequenceForThisManifest: DOM-37R, DOM-38R and DOM-39R all rest on this premise. A zod upgrade can silently invalidate the MEASUREMENT rather than fail the code, so a green run of these three after a zod bump is not evidence until the replica contract test is re-read.

precedingEvidence.what: Twelve mutants against the SAME invariants where they then lived: inline in the validate and publish steps of twi-orchestrator/src/workflow.ts and in twi-orchestrator/src/db.ts, run against the full Workflow integration suite twi-orchestrator/test/workflow.test.ts.
precedingEvidence.result: NINE of twelve SURVIVED. Only the two event-key mutants and the wrong-from-status transition died, because the happy path exercises those. The digest comparison, the provenance content-type, spec-digest and label matches, the provisional assertion, the both-candidates gate, the master header check, the provisional count comparison and the frozen-job digest check could each be deleted with the suite still green.
precedingEvidence.why: Those checks only fire on state the happy path cannot produce, and inline in a 200-line step there was no seam at which a test could forge a violation. The suite was not weak about what it covered; the code offered nothing to cover.
precedingEvidence.response: The predicates were extracted into twi-orchestrator/src/publication-guards.ts, which makes them forgeable by unit test (PUB-01 to PUB-13), and contract-check section 15 now reads the call graph of workflow.ts and db.ts to prove the guards are still INVOKED (PUB-14 to PUB-20). A unit test proves a predicate; only the call graph proves the call.

sets.result: 14 of 14 KILLED, measured by the committed harness. Every mutation was verified to have LANDED (sha256 compared before the suite ran) and restored byte-identically afterwards, because a mutation that fails to apply is indistinguishable from one that got killed - this project has been fooled that way three times.
sets.whatThisSetIsFor: Task 11 replaced the in-Worker fake finish step with a real Modal job, a waitForEvent per candidate and an authenticated callback route. Almost every guard it added fires only on state the happy path cannot produce - a forged callback, a replayed callback, a mastered archive, an object Modal never uploaded - which is the exact shape that let NINE of twelve publication mutants survive the full suite once before.

sets.title: Provider-call state - the ledger written before the billable call, and the retry gate that reads it (research P0)
sets.testCommand: per mutant, named in the harness: npm run test:twi:schema | npx vitest run --config vitest.twi.config.ts src/twi/server | npm test --prefix twi-orchestrator | npm run test:twi:contracts
sets.historicalNumbering: PCS-01 to PCS-20 at the provider-call-state round, PCS-21 to PCS-26 added in fix round 1, PCS-27 to PCS-32 added by the resolve-provider-call route round. No prior labels, no collisions, no id reused.
provenanceRounds: provider-call-state, 2026-09-02, on branch feat/twi-ambiguous-paid-call-state at cd87b87
provider-call-state fix round 1, 2026-09-03, on branch feat/twi-ambiguous-paid-call-state (base 586eabc) -- PCS-21 to PCS-26 added, all 26 re-measured in one campaign
sets.result: 26 of 26 KILLED, measured by the committed harness in one campaign at fix round 1 (TOTAL 26 KILLED 26 PROBLEMS 0, exit 0). Every mutation was verified to have LANDED (sha256 compared before any suite ran) and restored byte-identically afterwards, and the killing test names were extracted from each runner own output rather than retyped. PCS-14 survived every test suite and died ONLY in the contract check, by design: it is the measurement that section 16 pins the CALL and not the predicate. PCS-21 needs BOTH a suite and the contract check for the same reason -- the suite proves the refusal, the contract check proves the comparison is still there to make it. FIVE of the six entries added in fix round 1 are guards a verifier hand mutant SURVIVED in the first campaign (PCS-21 = VM-06, PCS-23 = VM-02, PCS-26 = V-01b) or guards that round added because of one (PCS-22, PCS-24, PCS-25), so this set now measures what the first campaign could not see.
sets.whatThisSetIsFor: The research P0 -- model not_submitted -> submitting -> accepted/completed plus ambiguous, persist the request id and the charge certainty, never auto-retry an ambiguous paid call -- landed as a D1 table written BEFORE the billable call, a step body whose order is claim -> pay -> settle, a retry gate that reads the ledger, and a human reconciliation primitive. Every one of those guards fires only on state the happy path never produces: a re-executed step body, a provider that failed with an unknown charge, a retry pressed after a paid attempt, a console writing an illegal pair. That is the exact shape that let nine of twelve publication mutants survive a green suite once before, so each guard here has a mutant that removes or weakens it and a named test that notices. Fix round 1 added the second lesson: three of the guards this set was built to protect had no mutant at all, and independent verifiers found them by hand. A guard with a test is not the same as a guard with a mutant, and only the mutant tells you the test would notice.
sets.supersedes: Nothing. This set adds behaviour that did not exist at 119ea66; no earlier entry is retired by it.

mutants.severity: schema invariant

target.construct: the table-level state/certainty pairing CHECK, deleted

mutation.find:
CONSTRAINT twi_provider_calls_state_certainty CHECK (
    (state = 'submitting' AND charge_certainty = 'unknown')
    OR (state = 'ambiguous' AND charge_certainty = 'unknown')
    OR (state = 'completed' AND charge_certainty = 'charged')
    OR (state = 'accepted' AND charge_certainty = 'charged')
    OR (state = 'abandoned' AND charge_certainty = 'not_charged')
  ),

killedBy.test: provider-call state and charge certainty are paired by the table, and every other pairing is refused

mutants.note: THE ONE THAT MATTERS MOST. With this CHECK gone a console, a script or a bug can store ambiguous/not_charged and the row stops blocking a retry while the money is still unaccounted for. Dies only in the schema suite, which drives the table with RAW SQL -- TypeScript can never produce an illegal pair, so no repository test can see this.

file. Everything else is transcribed from the reports with its provenance attached. The manifest is a
faithful, applicable index of the claims — not an independent re-measurement of them.

futureRunner.note: The owner chose a manifest, not an executable suite. This format is designed so a runner can consume it later without a rewrite. What such a runner would need:
alreadyProvided: A literal find/replace per mutant, with the anchor verified unique at the baseline commit.
The target file, the test command per set, and the expected outcome per mutant.
Named killing tests, so a runner can assert WHICH test failed rather than only that the suite went red.
Per-mutant multi-site support (`kind: multi-site`, `sites[]`) for the mutants that are one logical change at several places.
Explicit `expected` values including `known-survivor` and `retired`, so a runner does not report an accepted gap as a regression or try to apply a retired mutant.
stillNeeded: A SYNTAX GATE. A mutated file that no longer parses must be reported INVALID, not KILLED — group-e's first pass reported a false 79/79 because its deletion helper ate the comma terminating a column definition. This is why every schema CHECK mutant here is expressed as neutralize-to-`(1)` rather than deletion.
AN ANCHOR-UNIQUENESS PRECHECK at run time, aborting if `find` is missing or occurs more than once, so no mutant can silently half-apply. fence-parity's harness did exactly this.
A BASELINE GATE: refuse to run unless the suite is green first, and re-verify green after restoring.
RESTORE FROM AN IN-MEMORY SNAPSHOT, not from git, so a dirty tree cannot be destroyed. All three prior harnesses did this.

PER-MUTANT KILL SUITE, not per-set: SCH-HOUR24 targets the migration but is killed by `test:twi`, and `test:twi:schema` stays green under it. A runner keyed on target file would report a false survivor.
MUTANT-PAIR EXCLUSION: DOM-02/DOM-06 share an anchor, as do DOM-08/DOM-20. They must never be applied together.

TWO NON-find/replace APPLY MODES beyond plain substitution: `kind: delete-lines` with a `mechanicalRule` regex (SCH-M15, SCH-HOUR24 — both automatable, and SCH-HOUR24 was applied that way in this round's spot-check) and `kind: append` with a `payload` (MIG-01, MIG-02 — these mutate files OUTSIDE TWI and need their own byte-identity restore check).
A DECISION ON THE FOUR described-only ENTRIES (DOM-26, SCH-K05, REPO-04, REPO-06). They carry no applicable mutation at all and must be skipped-with-a-warning, never silently counted as passing.
COMMIT SCOPING. Entries carry `appliesAtCommit`; three target code that does not exist at the baseline. A runner must skip or check out accordingly rather than reporting them as missing anchors.

PREMISE CHECKING. Some entries carry a `premise` naming a dependency version (DOM-37R/38R/39R depend on zod 3.25.76 reading array elements in exactly one place). A runner should refuse to treat those results as evidence after a bump of the named dependency until the premise's own contract test is re-read — a changed premise invalidates the MEASUREMENT silently instead of failing the code.

AN EQUIVALENT-MUTANT VERDICT, separate from KILLED and SURVIVED. See retirementKinds.became-equivalent and DOM-32R.equivalenceHazard: a mutant made unkillable by construction reads as a survivor and must be retired explicitly, not scored and not deleted.
EXPANSION OF THE aggregate-only GROUPS (56 mutants across eight groups). Roughly 40 are mechanically enumerable from the migration itself; the rest need re-derivation.
futureRunner.costEstimate: Small. A ~150-line scripts/twi-mutants.mjs with readFileSync/JSON.parse, a spawnSync per suite, and the five gates above. No dependency. The reason not to build it now is not difficulty — it is that a runner over a manifest with six described-only entries and eight aggregate groups would report confident numbers over an incomplete set, which is the failure this file exists to stop.
